levers.how: Speak at the two September budget hearings at 5:01 p.m. in the Commission Chamber, 1700 Convention Center Drive, in person or on Zoom when the item is called (2026: Thursday Sept 10 and Wednesday Sept 23). The second hearing adopts the final millage (2026-34470), operating budget (2026-34471) and capital budget (2026-34474). Earlier: the Commission budget retreat (2026: May 5, 3:30 p.m.) and the Finance and Economic Resiliency Committee briefings (2026: June 17 and July 17).
levers.rules: Raise hand in Zoom or press *9 by phone; eComments and emails to CityClerk@miamibeachfl.gov accepted until 5:00 p.m. the day before. Citizens' Forum at regular meetings: 8:30 a.m. and 1:00 p.m., two minutes, no appointment needed.
levers.deadline: At the hearing; written comment by 5:00 p.m. the day before

levers.how: The proposed operating budget book (posted on the budget page in August) lists positions by department with the prior year; the adopted book follows in December. The FERC July 17, 2026 briefing discussed a $21 million gap, a flat millage rate and eliminating several vacant positions.
levers.rules: Books are PDFs under wp-content/uploads; the Budget in Brief summarizes position changes. Office of Management and Budget: 305-673-7510.

levers.how: Request payroll by employee or the full check register from the City Clerk: online portal, email researchrequest@miamibeachfl.gov, or 305.673.7000 ext. 26556.
levers.rules: 'Copies to be charged (if total exceeds $1.00)': $0.15 per one-sided copy, $1 per certified copy; a special service charge applies when labor is 'extensive', defined as 'labor of 1/2 hour or more'; 'the requester must provide payment in full before the City is required to produce the records.'

levers.how: Contract awards come to the Commission as agenda items (PrimeGov portal); speak when the item is called in person or on Zoom, or post an eComment.
levers.rules: eComment or email with the item number in the subject line, until 5:00 p.m. the day before. Presentation files to communications@miamibeachfl.gov by 8:30 a.m. one business day before.
levers.deadline: 5:00 p.m. the day before the meeting for written comment

levers.how: Each collective bargaining agreement is ratified by Commission resolution after the unit votes; the executed agreements are posted on the Employee and Labor Relations page. Four of five agreements (CWA, FOP, GSAF, IAFF) run through September 30, 2027, so successor bargaining falls in 2027.
levers.rules: Speak on the ratification item when called or send an eComment by 5:00 p.m. the day before.

levers.how: Report fraud, waste, abuse of power, mismanagement or corruption to the city's Office of Inspector General: hotline 786.897.1111, office 305.673.7020, CityofMiamiBeachOIG@miamibeachfl.gov, online form, or 1130 Washington Ave, 6th Floor. The OIG was created by charter amendment approved by 81% of voters on November 6, 2018 (Ordinance 2019-4239); it audits any city program, contract or expenditure, can subpoena records, and its reports are posted online. Internal audit (resort tax and contract audits) sits inside the OIG.
levers.rules: You 'may remain anonymous'; if you give your name it 'will be protected to the maximum extent of the law.' The Inspector General serves a four-year term and can be removed only by a 5/7 Commission vote.

notes: Staffing is empty: the city's robots.txt ('Disallow: /*.pdf$') blocks the fetch tool from every PDF, so the FY 2027 proposed and FY 2026 adopted operating budget books, the Budget in Brief, the City Manager's message, the FERC briefings, the ACFR and the adopted-budget resolutions (also Laserfiche at docmgmt.miamibeachfl.gov) could not be read, and no HTML page on the site prints position or payroll totals. The shell cannot reach miamibeachfl.gov. The FY 2024 vendor payments PDF was readable in one fetch before the block applied; its top 30 payees are listed, but the file prints no purpose or department column and no grand total, and it is alphabetical, so the ranking is from the rows the fetch returned (about 2,000 of them) and could miss a payee on an unread page. Several top payees are not vendors in the ordinary sense (pension funds, IRS deductions, the city itself, the County). No FY 2025 or FY 2026 vendor payments file was found. Union terms come from the posted file names on the labor relations page because the agreement PDFs are blocked; 'expires' assumes the city fiscal year end (September 30) for the 2027 and 2028 agreements, as printed for the FOP file. Commission vote dates on the CBAs were not captured. Cycle dates (May 5 retreat, Sept 10 and Sept 23 hearings) match scripts/data/cycles/city-miami-beach.json. Sources saved under scratchpad payments-src (mb-all.txt).
